# A package whose tests do not compile fails alone. The binary the packages
# share is linked once, without that package's tests, and every other package
# still runs, one of them importing the broken package itself.

! go test -x ./good ./broken ./user
stdout '^ok\s+example.com/broken/good'
stdout '^ok\s+example.com/broken/user'
stdout '^FAIL\s+example.com/broken/broken \[build failed\]'
stderr 'undefined: missing'
stderr -count=1 'link(\.exe)?"? -o'

# -c writes a copy for each package whose tests compile, and none for the
# package whose tests do not.
! go test -c -o $WORK/bin/ ./good ./broken ./user
exists $WORK/bin/good.test$GOEXE
exists $WORK/bin/user.test$GOEXE
! exists $WORK/bin/broken.test$GOEXE

-- go.mod --
module example.com/broken

go 1.27
-- good/good_test.go --
package good

import "testing"

func TestGood(test *testing.T) {}
-- broken/broken.go --
package broken

func Value() int { return 42 }
-- broken/broken_test.go --
package broken

import "testing"

func TestBroken(test *testing.T) {
	_ = missing
}
-- user/user_test.go --
package user

import (
	"testing"

	"example.com/broken/broken"
)

func TestUser(test *testing.T) {
	if broken.Value() != 42 {
		test.Fatal("broken.Value() != 42")
	}
}
